_readme: Grounded facts the AI features may use for DINO 15914. Every fact names its source. The AI is told to use these and nothing else, so add per-bone facts under `structures` only from the paper or the Dryad README, never from memory. Bone name, side and source file are added automatically from the manifest.

specimen.text: Helioscopos dickersonae is a Late Jurassic stem gekkotan (pan-gekkotan) based on a three-dimensionally preserved partial skull from the Morrison Formation of western North America.
Despite its Late Jurassic age, the species already possesses several key characteristics of the gekkotan skull along with retained ancestral features.
The holotype is DINO 15914, a partial skull and mandibles lacking the anterior snout, held at Dinosaur National Monument.
specimen.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

specimen.text: Preserved elements include the maxillae, prefrontals, parietal, right postorbitofrontal and squamosal, left jugal, partial palatines and right pterygoid, partial braincase, dentaries, and the fused left postdentary bones.
specimen.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

specimen.text: The genus name refers to a prominent pineal foramen (helios + scopós, 'sun-watcher'); the species honors Helen and Shirley Dickerson and Mary Cynthia Dickerson.
specimen.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

specimen.text: Fusion of the braincase (sphenoid–basioccipital contact indistinguishably fused) and fused surangular–prearticular indicate skeletal maturity of the holotype.
specimen.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

specimen.text: The 3D STLs in this viewer were segmented from microCT data collected at the University of Texas High-Resolution X-ray CT Facility and deposited in Dryad Set 3.

frontals.text: The frontals are paired and moderately constricted at their midpoint, a feature shared with other members of Ardeosauridae.
frontals.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

frontals.text: Each frontal has a prominent subolfactory process that arches ventromedially toward its counterpart but fails to meet on the midline, unlike the fused tubular condition of crown gekkotans.
frontals.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

parietal.text: The parietal table is nearly as long anteroposteriorly as it is wide mediolaterally, with a smooth dorsal surface lacking dermal rugosities.
parietal.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

parietal.text: A prominent pineal foramen perforates the centre of the parietal table; the diagnosis contrasts this with the smaller or absent foramen of some related taxa.
parietal.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

maxilla_l.text: The maxilla is anteroposteriorly longer than mediolaterally wide; the facial process rises at a high angle and the lateral margin bears a row of at least three mental foramina.
maxilla_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

maxilla_l.text: The maxilla has spaces for roughly 20 teeth with unicuspid, slightly recurved apices; the suborbital ramus tapers posteriorly and would have terminated in the anterior half of the orbit.
maxilla_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

maxilla_r.text: The right maxilla appears to preserve the entire suborbital ramus; medially, a palatal shelf extends over the tooth row and would have articulated with the palatine.
maxilla_r.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

dentary_l.text: The dentaries are dorsoventrally shallow and taper toward their anterior ends; each lateral surface has a row of four mental foramina of roughly equal size.
dentary_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

dentary_l.text: A thickened medial ridge underlies at least 16 unicuspid dentary teeth; Meckel's canal is exposed along the length of the dentary.
dentary_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

dentary_r.text: The right dentary shares the shallow, anteriorly tapering form of the left; the catalog notes that in the deposited meshes it lies apart from the main bone cluster (published positions preserved, not an articulated reconstruction).
dentary_r.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B / specimen catalog

compound_bone_l.text: The left prearticular and surangular are fused into a compound (postdentary) bone but lack their anterior and posterior ends.
compound_bone_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

compound_bone_l.text: This surangular–prearticular fusion is treated as a marker of skeletal maturity in the holotype.
compound_bone_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

braincase.text: The partial braincase is mediolaterally wide and slightly dorsoventrally compressed (possibly taphonomic); the occipital condyle has a transversely flat posterior margin in ventral view.
braincase.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

braincase.text: The sphenoid–basioccipital contact is fused indistinguishably, a marker of skeletal maturity in squamates used to interpret DINO 15914 as adult.
braincase.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

jugal_l.text: The left jugal is mediolaterally thin (possibly a taphonomic artefact) and smoothly arcuate, with a prominent maxillary ramus and a complete postorbital ramus that taper distally.
jugal_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

jugal_l.text: A quadratojugal process of the jugal is absent; the diagnosis describes the jugal as more gracile than that of Ardeosaurus brevipes.
jugal_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

prefrontal_l.text: The prefrontal is large and robust, with a long, tapering supraorbital process (the anterior process is broken).
prefrontal_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

prefrontal_l.text: Medially the prefrontal is bowed posteriorly to form the posterior border of the nasal capsule and has a vertical medial margin; the left prefrontal mesh lies apart from the main cluster in the deposited files.
prefrontal_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B / specimen catalog

prefrontal_r.text: Like the left, the right prefrontal is a large, robust element contributing to the orbital margin; facets on the frontal receive the prefrontal anteriorly.
prefrontal_r.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

postorbitofrontal_r.text: The postorbital and postfrontal are fused into a postorbitofrontal; it is anteroposteriorly elongate with tapering frontal and jugal processes.
postorbitofrontal_r.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

palatine_l.text: The palatines are incompletely preserved; they are smooth and edentulous, and ventrally bear a choanal fossa that arches strongly over the choana.
palatine_l.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

palatine_r.text: An appreciable portion of the pterygoid process of the palatine is preserved; edentulous palatines are shared with crown gekkotans, though the authors note this may be convergent.
palatine_r.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

pterygoid_r.text: The right pterygoid is partially preserved, showing the confluence of the palatine, transverse, and quadrate rami, though none of these processes are intact.
pterygoid_r.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

pterygoid_r.text: The transverse ramus is the thinnest of the three; a ridge runs along the ventral surface, and the pterygoid is edentulous like the palatines.
pterygoid_r.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B

squamosal_r.text: The right squamosal is preserved; the differential diagnosis contrasts Helioscopos with Ardeosaurus brevipes in having a narrower anterior squamosal among other skull-roof differences.
squamosal_r.source: Meyer et al. 2023, Proc. R. Soc. B
